severity_name: HEAVY SLOP WARNING — HERITAGE INTEGRITY ADVISORY
headline: HEAVY SLOP WARNING: COUNTERFEIT-NOSTALGIA FRONT SETTLES OVER FIVE REGIONS AS AI-GENERATED PHOTOGRAPHS OF A PAST THAT NEVER OCCURRED FARM SIGHS OF 'SIMPLER TIMES' FROM RESIDENTS WHO CORRECTLY REMEMBER THAT IT WAS, IN FACT, NOT LIKE THAT
advisory: A warm, low-pressure system of manufactured yesteryear has stalled over the Facebook Delta and is expected to persist through the week. Residents are advised that sepia-toned images captioned '1962 — nobody locked their doors' are frequently synthetic, and that the reassuring haze around the edges is a rendering artifact, not the mist of memory. The National Slop Service reminds the public that a real photograph of the past will not contain a car with eleven doors, and that genuine nostalgia does not require an engagement prompt reading 'Type AMEN if you miss this.'

regional_outlook.conditions: Dense heritage fog throughout, with visibility reduced to one generation. Expect standing pools of 'they don't make 'em like this anymore' beneath photographs of appliances that were never manufactured.
Warm currents of impossible farmhouse kitchens and 1950s diners rendered in flawless, load-bearing wood. Boards flooded with vintage recipes for dishes no one has cooked.
Groundwater contamination as fabricated 'historical photos' seep into image results and are cited as sources. Fact-checking runoff is minimal and arriving late.
Rapid downstream flow of 'restored footage' compilations set to melancholy piano. Watermarks visible only to those who slow the current to 0.25x.
Forwarded-chain surge as the front reaches residents by email. Subject lines gusting to 'FWD: FWD: Remember When Things Were REAL.'

specimen.status: Abundant; migratory into every family group chat by Sunday.
specimen.habitat: Sunlit patches of the Facebook Delta, particularly pages titled 'The Good Old Days' administered by no one in particular from a time zone eight hours ahead.
specimen.field_marks: Uniform golden haze; suspiciously symmetrical crowds; hands with a variable and generous number of fingers; storefront signage spelled with confident, invented letters. Always accompanied by a caption asserting a moral decline that the image alone cannot support.
specimen.call: 1948. Neighbors were neighbors. Sadly, this generation will never understand. ❤️ Type AMEN.
specimen.confusion_species: The genuine family archive photo, which it closely mimics. Tell them apart by the details: real snapshots have a specific date, a named relative, and at least one person squinting or blinking, whereas the Mirage renders everyone flawlessly wistful and no one at all real.

spotter_tip: Zoom in on the background text — a chalkboard menu, a shop awning, a newspaper. Authentic history spells 'BAKERY'; the Sepia Mirage spells 'BARKERYY' in a font that has never existed and charges $0.0Ⳮ for bread.
tomorrow: Nostalgia fog lifts slightly by afternoon, replaced by inbound 'you won't believe what this abandoned mansion looked like' drizzle across the Shorts Gorge.
